carousels.name: A wet dream on Day 18 isn't a relapse

slides.title: Woke up after a wet dream on Day 18? [[That's not a p*rn relapse.]]
slides.sub: Stop resetting your counter for something you didn't choose.

slides.title: Your body does it [[on its own]]
slides.body: Wet dreams are a normal body process, especially when you stop releasing regularly. You didn't open p*rn. You didn't decide anything.

slides.title: Relapse is a [[choice]]
slides.body: A relapse means choosing p*rn — searching, clicking, watching. Sleeping isn't a choice. Don't punish yourself for it.

slides.title: The real danger: [["screw it"]]
slides.body: Many guys wake up, think "well, I already failed," and open p*rn that morning. That's where the actual relapse happens.

slides.title: If it happens [[tonight]]
items: Get up and start your morning normally.
Stay away from p*rn — that's the only rule that matters.

carousels.name: Doing NNN in a relationship: 5 things your partner should know

slides.title: Quitting p*rn this November while in a relationship? [[Tell your partner these 5 things.]]
slides.sub: So she doesn't take your NNN personally.

slides.title: Tell her [[1–2]]
items: "This is about p*rn, not about you." She may wonder if she's the problem. She isn't.
"I'm not pulling away from you." Quitting p*rn can make you moody for a while — say it before she has to guess.

slides.title: Tell her [[3–4]]
items: "I want to be closer to you, not further." Real intimacy is part of why you're quitting.
"I might have rough days." Ask for patience, not supervision.

slides.title: Tell her [[5]]
items: "Here's why I'm really doing it." One honest sentence about your p*rn habit beats a month of silence.

slides.title: Open beats [[hidden]].
slides.body: A partner who understands what you're doing can support you. A partner left guessing fills the gap with worry. Say it out loud.

carousels.name: When one partner watches p*rn and the other doesn't (1,755 couples)

slides.title: He watches p*rn. She doesn't. [[Researchers found that gap matters.]]
slides.sub: What a study of 1,755 couples showed.

slides.title: Couples [[studied]]
slides.body: Willoughby and colleagues (2016) found that bigger differences in partners' p*rn use were linked to lower relationship satisfaction and stability.

slides.title: It shows up in [[how you talk]]
slides.body: The same study linked a bigger p*rn gap to less positive communication and more conflict. It's not just about sex — it's about how you treat each other.

slides.title: Why the gap [[hurts]]
slides.body: One partner feels compared, left out or lied to. The other feels judged or defensive. Nobody talks — and the distance grows.

slides.title: Close the [[gap]]
items: Talk about p*rn before it becomes a fight.
Stop hiding it — hidden use breaks trust fastest.
Get a counselor if you keep circling the same argument.

carousels.name: 5 things to do when a p*rn urge hits during the day

slides.kicker: At work, in class, on a break
slides.title: The p*rn urge hits at 2 PM — at work. [[5 things to do in the next 5 minutes.]]
slides.sub: Daytime urges need different tools than nighttime ones.

slides.title: Change your [[posture]]
slides.body: Stand up. Roll your shoulders. Walk to get water. Your body leads your brain — a 60-second walk can break the p*rn loop.

slides.title: Go where people [[are]]
slides.body: Kitchen, common room, a colleague's desk. Urges shrink fast around other humans.

slides.title: Do the [[hardest]] task
slides.body:
Daytime p*rn urges are often avoidance in disguise.

Open the task you're dodging and do 5 minutes of it.

slides.title: Tips [[4–5]]
items: Text a funny friend — laughter resets your mood fast.
Plan your evening now — the daytime urge often signals a risky night ahead.

carousels.name: Stop googling whether p*rn is bad for you

slides.title: Stop googling "is p*rn bad for me?" [[You're looking for permission, not answers.]]
slides.sub: You already know. That's why you're searching.

slides.title: The [[permission]] search
slides.body: You're hoping one article says "it's fine, relax." Then you can keep watching p*rn without guilt. That's the real reason you search.

slides.title: Your life is the [[evidence]]
slides.body: Your sleep. Your focus. Your confidence. Your relationships. Your hiding. That's better data than any article.

slides.title: Ask a better [[question]]
slides.body: Not "is p*rn bad for everyone?" But "is p*rn good for me — honestly?"

slides.title: Answer it [[honestly]]
items: Write down 3 things p*rn has cost you.
